numerical_failure.observed_behavior: During Period conversion from a timestamp at millisecond or microsecond resolution near the minimum timestamp, overflow checking fails due to negative-side overflow/underflow while scaling the time to the smaller unit; the fix introduces split scaling logic that avoids underflow/overflow in checked_mul/checked_add, indicating the bug manifests as an overflow-check failure that raises an exception.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Correct recoverable handling (no erroneous overflow during scaling) for near-minimum timestamps with microsecond and millisecond resolutions when converting periods from timestamps.
trigger_conditions: Near-minimum timestamps (negative-side overflow/underflow during scaling) during Period conversion from timestamps
oracle_clues: PR title/description: "BUG: handle negative overflow in Period conversion from timestamp with millisecond resolution".

Code/logic: helper is introduced to "Handle underflow when scaling time to a smaller unit" and splits computation using y = a * x + b = a * (x + k) + (b - a * k) to avoid underflow/overflow from checked_* functions.

Helper failure mode: "Returns false on success, true on failure (from checked_* functions)." Call site uses PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW(scale_time_with_underflow_check(...)), indicating an overflow-check failure/exception rather than a silently wrong numeric result.
What’s new entry: "Fixed recoverable overflow for near-minimum timestamps with microsecond and millisecond resolutions" (:issue:`63278`).

Updated conversions: in the ms case, the previous direct checked_mul/checked_add path (scaleSecondsToMilliseconds + checked_add) is replaced with PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW(scale_time_with_underflow_check(seconds, 1000L, dts->us/1000L, &milliseconds)).
In the us case, the previous conditional underflow-splitting logic is replaced with PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW(scale_time_with_underflow_check(seconds, 1000000L, dts->us, &microseconds)).

category_specific_evidence: The helper function is introduced specifically to “Handle underflow when scaling time to a smaller unit,” noting that scaling can otherwise “avoid underflow, if necessary, in the following manner: y = a * x + b = a * (x + k - k) + b = a * (x + k) + (b - a * k)”.
The failure mode it addresses is overflow/checked failure during scaling/addition: “Returns false on success, true on failure (from checked_* functions).”

The corrected computation uses a threshold derived from int64 limits: const int64_t min_scalable_time = NPY_MIN_INT64 / scale_factor; and if time < min_scalable_time it computes amount_below_threshold = time - min_scalable_time, then sets scaled_time = scale_factor * (time - amount_below_threshold), and combines via checked_mul/checked_add in split form.

A concrete mathematical identity underlying the reproduction requirement is explicitly shown as the split: a*x + b is evaluated via a*(x+k) + (b - a*k) to prevent numerical underflow/checked overflow during scaling to smaller units.
The Period conversion bug scenario being targeted is stated as: “BUG: handle negative overflow in Period conversion from timestamp with millisecond resolution”.

A test reproducer is added that constructs Period from Timestamp at the minimum timestamp value for frequencies 'ms', 'us', 'ns': ts = Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit=freq) and per = Period(ts, freq=freq), with the test referencing GH-63278 (min timestamp).
reproduction_risks: Reproduction may require constructing values at the minimum representable timestamp (Timestamp.min.value / NPY_MIN_INT64 regime), since the fix is gated on time < NPY_MIN_INT64 / scale_factor.

Reproduction likely needs negative-time/negative overflow behavior because the bug is described as “negative overflow” and the underflow handling is for scaling to smaller units near the minimum int64 time.
Reproduction should include millisecond resolution specifically (freq='ms'), because the bug annotation targets “timestamp with millisecond resolution,” and the test parameterizes ['ms','us','ns'].
Without matching the checked arithmetic pathways (scale_time_with_underflow_check / checked_mul / checked_add), reproductions may not trigger the underflow-split logic.

provenance.value: A recoverable integer overflow/recoverable error occurred during Period conversion from a timestamp when scaling time to millisecond and microsecond resolutions near the minimum timestamp (negative overflow case). The fix introduces checks to handle underflow/overflow safely during scaling by splitting the computation when the input is below a minimum threshold.
Correct recoverable handling (no erroneous overflow during scaling) for near-minimum timestamps with millisecond and microsecond resolution when converting periods from timestamps.
